data.narrative:
Cognichip is a Series A semiconductor company founded by Faraj Aalaei that has raised $93M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 8 private and 3 public semiconductor companies, including same-stage comparables SambaNova Systems ($11.0B), Rebellions ($2.3B), and d-Matrix ($2.0B), as well as public benchmarks NVDA, AMD, and ALAB.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x multiplier to the $93M total raised, implying a $186M valuation. Peer-median analysis across the three same-sector, same-stage private comparables yields a median valuation of $2.3B, with a range spanning $2.0B to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (sector median 20.5x) cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures. The wide dispersion among private peers—particularly SambaNova's $11.0B outlier—reflects heterogeneous market assessments within the chip sector at Series A.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $158M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.3B. The stage-progression method anchors the lower bound; peer multiples drive the higher bound. Key uncertainties include Cognichip's disclosed revenue or ARR, technical differentiation relative to the peer set, and whether early funding velocity merits premium or discount to the peer median. Without revenue visibility, the wide range reflects material estimation risk.
